Analysis.object: The results support the protective role of positive body image preventing dysfunctional eating in adolescent girls of various sports practice and in competitive sports involved boys.

The cross sectional design does not lead to understanding the direction of the associations between the study variables. The associations between body appreciation and disordered eating in sports involved adolescents might be mediated by the quality of motivation, with external motivation providing less favourable eating behaviour outcome. The self reported status of sport participation might also be considered as a limitation. We did not assess the level of participation in competitive sports. Elite sports-involved adolescents might significantly differ in body image and dysfunctional eating characteristics.

Disordered eating prevention programs should include education about the importance of body appreciation and functionality. 
Future studies might benefit from including athletes whom formally participate in professional sports.
